name: apps
title: Applications
description: Launch any installed app by name, with its own icon. On macOS, running apps can be quit or hidden and the System Settings panes are rows too; on Linux, an app's own actions are one key away.
author: pal

settings.label: Extra folders
settings.description: Scanned in addition to the system's application folders.

store.tagline: Every installed app, with its icon, a keystroke from launch
features: Every app in your Applications folders on macOS, every `.desktop` entry and flatpak on Linux
Found by name or bundle id, so `Chrome` or `com.apple.` both work
Running apps are tagged, with Quit (`cmd+q`) and Hide (`cmd+h`)
System Settings panes as rows on macOS, found by words like `dark mode` or `dns`
On Linux, an app's own actions (`New Private Window`) as secondary actions
`cmd+i` shows where it lives, its version, bundle id and processes

screenshots.caption: The applications by name, the running ones tagged
Typing at the root finds an app by its bundle id as well as its name: ical is Calendar (com.apple.iCal)
A running app: Open, Quit, Hide, Reveal in Finder, Copy path, Copy bundle id
The System Settings panes are rows too, found by what they hold: network finds Network and Wi-Fi
An app's details (cmd+i): its folder, running and its version, the bundle id and processes

actions.title: Quit
actions.description: Asks the app through AppleScript, so it may ask you to save; a toast when it is not running.

actions.title: Copy URL
actions.description: On a System Settings pane: its x-apple.systempreferences: link.

keys.title: Copy the path (a pane: its URL)
